verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — X wins narrowly on three specific verified findings Y lacks, all load-bearing for the brief's "ground every claim in CODE, not comments" instruction. (1) X found that wrap-ledger.sh:1985-1986 renders the 📦 rung as "Land IN FLIGHT … do NOT fire a second /ship" while ship_floor reads only RUNG/TRUNK/AHEAD/SHAS (confirmed: the only greps into $led are :1127, :1148, :1181-1182) and therefore blocks with "/ship it NOW" — a real contradiction between the two surfaces. (2) X flagged wrap-ledger.sh:25's header definition of 🔧 as stale against the live ladder (:1941-1961 removes the gate term; :1997-2052 adds six more 🔧 sources); Y states the correct 🔧 list but never flags the stale line. (3) X verified by grep that session-continue.sh:1082-1083's quotation of the mechanical header ("📦 must NOT fire") no longer exists at :897-929. X also uniquely names the "no jq ⇒ .count increments but nothing prints" case and the payload-field census (only .cwd/.session_id/.transcript_path; stop_hook_active never read). Y's counterweights are real but smaller: the legacy no-pid branch of mailbox_wake_armed (mailbox-pending.sh:299), fuller agent-identity seams, and X's one soft error (§9's CLAUDE_SESSION_ID inference ignores wrap-ledger.sh:640's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID fallback — though X labels that section unverified). Both produced essentially the same verified stale-citation table and both independently refuted the in-file :963-966 claim that the wake floor's assignee policy differs (code: all three exempt on rc 0|2, none on rc 1 — :780-784, :970, :1105).

X vs Z — X wins decisively. Z carries two materially wrong code claims: that ${f}.count is "reset to absent only by an explicit CLI set" (it is also removed at :1206, :253, :1229, :1247, :1260 — and the :1206 deletion is exactly the mechanism behind the product bound Z itself quotes), and that RUNG=🔧 means "dirty ∨ gate stale ∨ remainder" on the authority of the stale comment at wrap-ledger.sh:25, which the brief expressly warned against. Z also reports the teardown-marker divergence backwards ("consistent"), when wf_teardown_marked :551-568 omits the '"mode":"teardown"' test retired_by_desk :258 requires. Z missed the :963-966 falsehood, the missing digit guards, the no-pane-id custody fallback at :762-764, and declared the Stop-chain position claim unverifiable "anywhere reachable" when settings-templates/settings.example.json:466/:476 confirms it in-snapshot. X has none of these and adds the verified LANDING contradiction.

Y vs Z — Y wins on the same specifics. Y's two soft imperfections (the local overstatement "no mailbox state is consulted" on Arm A's trigger, and the same missed settings.example.json) are far smaller than Z's two wrong code claims and its inverted reading of the teardown marker. Y additionally verified the exact rc-2 enumerations in session-writes.sh, the agent-identity seam defaults, the no-digit-guard asymmetry, the bare-shell-clear sid-'?' interaction with :1060, and the :963-966 comment's falsity — all absent from Z. Z's genuine advantages (the ship-floor sha-latch accumulation reading, the silent-budget contrast at :1096, the hook-chain not-wired caveat) are also present or matched in Y.
